verses.text: Jesus called the twelve together and gave them power and authority over all demons and to heal diseases.
He sent them out to announce God’s Kingdom and heal the sick.
He told them, “Take nothing for the road: no walking stick, bag, bread, or money. Don’t bring a spare shirt.”
“When you enter a house, stay there until you leave that town.”
“If people won’t welcome you, leave that town and shake even its dust from your feet as a witness against them.”
The disciples set out and traveled through the villages, sharing the good news and healing people everywhere.
Herod the ruler heard about everything happening through Jesus and was confused. Some people were saying John had risen from the dead,
others said Elijah had appeared, and still others said one of the prophets from long ago had come back.
Herod said, “I had John beheaded, so who is this I keep hearing about?” He kept trying to see Jesus.
When the apostles returned, they told Jesus everything they had done. He took them along and slipped away to a deserted area near Bethsaida.
But the crowds found out and followed him. Jesus welcomed them, taught them about God’s Kingdom, and healed those who needed it.
The day was getting late. The twelve came to him and said, “Send the crowd away to nearby villages and farms to find food and a place to stay. We’re out in the middle of nowhere.”
But Jesus said, “You give them something to eat.” They replied, “We have only five loaves and two fish—unless we go buy food for all these people.”
There were about five thousand men. Jesus told his disciples, “Have them sit in groups of about fifty.”
They did that and got everyone seated.
Jesus took the five loaves and two fish, looked up to heaven, blessed them, broke them, and gave them to the disciples to serve the crowd.
Everyone ate and was satisfied. The disciples gathered twelve baskets of leftover pieces. 🍞
One day, while Jesus was praying alone and the disciples were nearby, he asked them, “Who do the crowds say I am?”
They answered, “John the Baptizer. Others say Elijah, and some say a prophet from long ago has come back.”
He asked them, “And who do you say I am?” Peter answered, “God’s Christ.”
Jesus warned them and ordered them not to tell anyone.
He said, “The Son of Man must suffer many things. The elders, chief priests, and legal teachers will reject him. He’ll be killed, and on the third day he’ll be raised.”
Then he said to everyone, “If anyone wants to follow me, they must say no to themselves, pick up their cross, and follow me.”
“Whoever tries to save their life will lose it. But whoever loses their life for my sake will save it.”
“What good is it to gain the whole world if you lose yourself or ruin your life?”
“Whoever is ashamed of me and my words, the Son of Man will be ashamed of them when he comes in his glory, the Father’s glory, and the glory of the holy angels.”
“I’m telling you the truth: some people standing here won’t die before they see God’s Kingdom.”
About eight days later, Jesus took Peter, John, and James with him up the mountain to pray.
As he prayed, his face changed, and his clothes became dazzling white.
Suddenly, two men—Moses and Elijah—were talking with him.
They appeared in glory and spoke about Jesus’ departure, which he was about to accomplish in Jerusalem.
Peter and those with him were heavy with sleep. But when they woke up fully, they saw Jesus’ glory and the two men standing with him.
As Moses and Elijah were leaving, Peter said to Jesus, “Master, it’s good we’re here. Let’s build three shelters—one for you, one for Moses, and one for Elijah.” He didn’t know what he was saying.
While he was still speaking, a cloud came and covered them. They were afraid as the cloud surrounded them.
A voice came from the cloud: “This is my beloved Son. Listen to him!”
When the voice had spoken, Jesus was there alone. The disciples kept quiet and didn’t tell anyone then what they had seen.
The next day, when Jesus and the disciples came down from the mountain, a huge crowd met him.
A man in the crowd shouted, “Teacher, please look at my son! He’s my only child.”
“A spirit grabs him, and he suddenly screams. It throws him into convulsions until he foams at the mouth. It keeps hurting him badly and hardly ever leaves him.”
“I begged your disciples to drive it out, but they couldn’t.”
Jesus answered, “You unbelieving and twisted generation! How long must I stay with you and put up with this? Bring your son here.”
As the boy was coming, the demon threw him down and convulsed him violently. But Jesus rebuked the unclean spirit, healed the boy, and returned him to his father.
Everyone was amazed by God’s greatness. While they were still marveling at everything Jesus did, he told his disciples:
“Listen carefully: the Son of Man is about to be handed over to people.”
But they didn’t understand what he meant. It was hidden from them, and they were afraid to ask him about it.
Then an argument started among them about which one was the greatest.
Jesus knew what they were reasoning in their hearts. He took a little child and stood the child beside him.
He told them, “Whoever welcomes this child in my name welcomes me. And whoever welcomes me welcomes the one who sent me. The least among you all—that person is great.”
John said, “Master, we saw someone driving out demons in your name, and we tried to stop him because he doesn’t follow with us.”
Jesus told him, “Don’t stop him. Whoever isn’t against us is for us.”
As the time drew near for Jesus to be taken up, he firmly set his face toward Jerusalem
and sent messengers ahead. They entered a Samaritan village to get things ready for him.
But the people there wouldn’t welcome him, because he was headed for Jerusalem.
When his disciples James and John saw this, they said, “Lord, should we call fire down from heaven to destroy them, like Elijah did?”
Jesus turned and rebuked them: “You don’t know what kind of spirit you’re acting from.”
“The Son of Man didn’t come to destroy people’s lives, but to save them.” Then they went to another village.
As they continued on the road, someone said to Jesus, “Lord, I’ll follow you wherever you go.”
Jesus told him, “Foxes have dens, and birds have nests, but the Son of Man has nowhere to lay his head.”
He told another person, “Follow me.” But the man said, “Lord, first let me go bury my father.”
Jesus said, “Let the dead bury their own dead. You go and announce God’s Kingdom.”
Someone else said, “I’ll follow you, Lord, but first let me say goodbye to my family at home.”
Jesus told him, “No one who puts a hand to the plow and keeps looking back is fit for God’s Kingdom.”
